scope: iPhone-first touch, cancellation, real target sizes, and noneditable content protection

rules.target_implementation: 84rpx times the measured 393/viewport-width scale, rounded upward to avoid falling below 44 after rendering; actual targets, not overlapping pseudo-elements
rules.long_press: Recognized as a transient held presentation state; no new long-press business menu or automatic submission is invented.
rules.accepted_apple_purchases: Continue original account-bound recovery; page/gesture cancellation does not claim Apple payment cancellation.

implementation: One App-installed presentation policy blocks noneditable contextmenu, dragstart and selectstart, suppresses cancelled compatibility clicks, and clears press/hold state on pointer cancellation, capture loss, second touch, background and route changes.
No global touchmove/pointerdown prevention or touch-action:none was added. Native scroll ownership remains available; only the existing fixed Discover card owns its horizontal drag surface.

Actual DOM input and textarea nodes receive a presentation marker because uni-app rewrites raw input CSS selectors to component wrappers. Editable controls retain cursor, selection and unblocked copy/paste/beforeinput/composition events.

Dynamically mounted noneditable images are marked draggable=false. CSS disables normal callouts and system image dragging; WKWebView disables link previews without disabling its text-interaction preference or all long-press recognizers.

Discover uses separate start and continuation locks: its own dragging state blocks duplicate clicks but does not cancel the already owned swipe. External navigation, skeleton, settling and reset locks still cancel.
A fresh Discover touch clears only the prior swipe's time guard; the swipe's own compatibility click remains suppressed. Swipe, profile entry and return preserve the current person.

Home refresher, Profile question browsing and the voice progress slider share a single-pointer cancellation controller. Vertical intent wins in scrolling regions. Audio dragging previews locally and seeks once only on release, never on cancellation.

Shared writes reserve busy synchronously before watchers can reenter, recheck cancellation before an already queued timer can execute, settle cancelled Promises, and remove lifecycle listeners on unmount.

Important back/close/more/send/record/play controls and switches have real minimum touch targets. Settings switches keep their original painted track in a separate larger hit region. Dense visual indicators are not enlarged using overlapping invisible layers.
Group chat and the registered legacy messages entry receive missing busy/disabled semantics without a business-model or UI redesign.

actual_browser_touch_events: Hold does not click; touchCancel releases the state; a fresh touchscreen tap activates once.
Cancelled Discover swipe keeps the person, completed horizontal swipe advances once.
The next deliberate tap enters that profile immediately; returning retains that card.
Home scrolls with an actual vertical touch gesture after its first skeleton, in a short viewport with real overflowing content.
browser.important_target_measurements: At least 44 logical CSS points across tested widths, including Back and switch hit regions; icons/tracks keep their own visual dimensions.
browser.warning_boundary: The isolated browser intentionally aborts external traffic. The existing uni statistics SDK reports failed telemetry/retry warnings; these are retained in the report, not replaced with a fake server success. No unrelated application warnings were accepted.

wkwebview.warnings: Existing Xcode AppIntents metadata extraction and simulator WebKit/accessibility advisory logs do not prevent the passing targeted tests. No private entitlement was added.

limits: This suppresses App-owned default browser interactions, not screenshots, external access to resources, DRM or every possible OS-level image recognition feature.

Native automated tests verify real WKWebView styles, editable selection/ranges, event boundaries and retained native text interaction. They do not claim a manually operated system clipboard/menu matrix or physical-device keyboard/IME certification.
The existing whole-App visual/page acceptance and formal signing, real StoreKit purchase and push-service release dependencies remain separate.
worktree: Preexisting and staged user changes remain intact. No git add, commit, push or reset was performed; the existing dirty workspace is not represented as a clean project.
processes: Bounded build/test commands only. Temporary browser contexts close in finally; no preview service or watcher was started, and unrelated simulators/services were not stopped.
